newsitem.title: USA: IMF sees perils, promise in Latin America banks.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees perils, promise in Latin America banks.

text.p: Brazil's banking system is under pressure because of the government's continuing efforts to stabilise the country's economy, an International Monetary Fund report on global capital markets said on Wednesday.
High real interest rates and reserve requirements, coupled with a recession in mid-1995, have combined to put pressure on the system, the largest in Latin America, it said.
"Although the banking system has been under pressure, it appears to contain a core segment, consisting of large and medium-sized private banks, that is essentially sound," the report added.
Turning elsewhere in Latin America, the IMF said Mexico's banking system has been substantially stabilized through considerable government support, though it remain fragile.
"Although the banking system remains burdened by a significant volume of non-performing loans, by the end of 1995 the banking system had been substantially stabilised," the report said.
It said that the overall performance of the Argentine banking sector has improved but added that the Venezuelan government's costs of propping up its banks could increase further this year.
